 ZONING REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA  JULY 14, 2026

Members of the public wishing to make public comment may do so in one of the following ways:

(1) By directly addressing the Zoning Review Committee in person at the time(s) allotted on the agenda
for such comment. Persons wishing to address the Zoning Review Committee in person are asked to
fill out a speaker card providing their name and indicating whether they wish to address the Zoning
Review Committee on an item(s) of business appearing under (i) the Public Hearing portion of the
agenda; (ii) any item of business appearing under any other portion of the agenda; and/or (iii) a non-
agendized matter that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Zoning Review Committee.
Speaker cards should be submitted to City Staff prior to the Zoning Review Committee’s approval of
the agenda, if possible; or

(2) Email or Telephone – All interested parties can submit comments in advance to the Planning
Division’s general email at planning@elmonteca.gov or by calling the City’s telephone line: (626) 258-
8626. All comments must be received by the Planning Division no later than 3:00 pm on July 14, 2026.

Instruction regarding accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act can be found
on the last page of this Agenda.

 ZONING REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA  JULY 14, 2026

  General explanation of how the meeting is conducted:
  1. The staff report is presented by City Planning staff.
  2. The Zoning Review Committee may ask questions if necessary for clarification.
  3. The Zoning Review Committee Chair opens the public hearing.
  4. The applicant makes a presentation to the Zoning Review Committee.
  5. Individuals speaking in favor of the project address the Committee.
  6. Individuals speaking against the project address the Committee.
  7. The applicant responds to project opponents.
  8. The public hearing is closed.
  9. Zoning Review Committee members discuss the project.
  10. Zoning Review Committee members vote on the project.
  11. Any interested party who disagrees with the Zoning Review Committee decision may appeal the
  Committee’s decision to the Planning Commission within 10 calendar days. Any appeal filed must
  be directed to the City Clerk’s Office and must be accompanied by a fee of $1020.75 or $1,725.62
  (depending on the type of project). Any individual that received notice of this meeting from the City
  of El Monte will receive notice of an appeal if one is filed.

DATE:  July 14, 2026

TO:  Zoning Review Committee

FROM:  Steve Fowler, Community and Economic Development Director

APPLICATIONS:  Minor Use Permit (MUP) No. 15-2025 & Director Level Zoning

PROJECT/APPLICANT INFORMATION:

Subject Property: 2517 Tyler Avenue / APN 8104-019-039
Project Applicant & Property Owner: Danny Wonn

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:

The Applicant is requesting MUP No. 15-2025 to establish a vehicle repair facility
consisting of “Vehicle Repair, Minor” as defined in the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC)
to allow for general auto repair and maintenance services within an existing 4,800 square-
foot commercial building. Additionally, DLZC No. 13-2026 is requested to establish shared
access and parking with the adjacent northern parcel. The subject site is 19,200 square
feet in area and located in the M-1 (Light Manufacturing) zone. The MUP request is made
pursuant to Chapter 17.123 (Conditional and Minor Use Permits) of the El Monte Municipal
Code (EMMC). The DLZC request is made pursuant to Chapter 17.120 (Zoning
Clearances and Business Permits) of the EMMC.

 BACKGROUND:

The subject site is developed with a 4,800 square foot commercial building located on a
19,200-square-foot parcel. The existing structure was constructed in 1966. City records
reflect previous uses include auto repair, auto parts retail, and wholesale auto dealer.

ENTITLEMENTS REQUESTED:

The following entitlement is requested pursuant to the requirements of Section 17.123
Conditional and Minor Use Permits of the EMMC:

  •  Minor Use Permit (MUP) No. 15-2025, establishment of a vehicle repair- minor
  facility consisting of general auto repair and maintenance services – within an
  existing 4,800 square foot commercial building in the M-1 zone.

  •  Director Level Zoning Clearance (DLZC) No. 12-2026, establish shared parking
  with an adjacent parcel.

Minor vehicle repair uses are defined as facilities that provide mechanical repair, brakes
and tires services for automobiles, motorcycles, trucks (up to 16,000 pounds or Class 4),
and/or recreational vehicles. Staff determined that the vehicle repair minor facility is
consistent with the City of El Monte General Plan and the EMMC requirements with an
approved Minor Use Permit, as determined in the findings.

PROJECT CHARACTERISTICS:

Business Operations
The operations statement describes the proposed use as an auto repair facility that will
provide a range of automotive services, including, but not limited to, oil changes, tire
rotations, engine diagnostics, and exhaust and suspension repairs.

The proposed hours of operation are as follows:

  •  Monday through Friday -8:00AM-6:30PM
  •  Saturday - 9:00AM-3:00PM
  •  Sunday - Closed

The auto repair business will have four (4) vehicle service bays, that will consist of car lifts,
a portable framing machine, and an alignment machine within the existing structure. No
additional square footage is proposed as part of this request.

The business anticipates employing four (4) to six (6) employees, including technicians,
service advisors, and administrative staff. Deliveries are anticipated to occur two (2) to
three (3) times per week to deliver auto parts and shop supplies via box truck or vans. No
large freight or semi-trailer deliveries are anticipated.

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 5
 Site Circulation & Parking
Ingress/egress to the subject site is provided from one (1) existing driveway along Tyler
Avenue. A total of 12 on-site parking spaces are provided for the building, including two
(2) accessible parking stalls.

Per the EMMC Section 17.70 (Parking Regulations), vehicle service uses require two (2)
spaces per service bay and one (1) space per 350 square feet of any retail and office area.
The proposed business consists of four (4) service bays (8 spaces required), 621 square
feet of office/retail area (2 spaces required), and 629 square feet of attic spaces (2 spaces),
requiring a total of 12 on-site parking spaces for customer parking. The applicant has
designated areas for parking that will be used for vehicles awaiting services, ensuring the
12 spaces will be available for customers.

The adjacent parcel to the north (APN: 8104-019-005) is owned by the same property
owner as the subject site and shares public right-of-way access from the driveway
referenced above. DLZC No. 13-2026 is meant to establish shared parking between both
sites to accommodate a potential future tenant established on the adjacent parcel.
Condition of Approval No. 25 will formalize a covenant to be recorded against the subject
site and the adjacent northern parcel in order to establish shared access and parking to
the existing driveway approach leading to the public right-of-way.

Floor Plan
The proposed floor plan (see Exhibit 2) illustrates the layout of the 4,800 square foot tenant
space. The building contains four (4) service bays with car lifts, an alignment machine,
and framing machine. Adjacent to the service bays, the offices and the waiting area are to
be used by customers and administrative staff.

Lot Merger
All new vehicle repair facilities, whether a primary or an ancillary use, are subject to the
specific requirements listed under EMMC 17.112.200. The development standards require
the subject site to be a minimum of 15,000 square feet and have minimum lot width of 80
linear feet. Three (3) parcels adjacent to one another, are under the same ownership of
which two (2) will be utilized for the proposed vehicle repair business. The applicant has
pursued and completed a lot merger under MAP-000018-2025 to merge 2517 and 2521
Tyler to meet minimum lot size and lot width as required.

PROJECT ANALYSIS:

General Plan Consistency
The subject property has a General Plan land use designation of “Industrial Business
Park”, that encourages a mix of sustainable manufacturing, processing, warehousing, and
distribution uses that generate employment, minimize traffic, and are compatible with
residential neighborhoods. The proposed minor vehicle repair use is consistent with the
following General Plan Land Use policies:

  Policy LU-1.1 Code Compliance. Ensure land use compatibility through adherence
  to the policies, standards, and regulations in the Municipal Code, Development
  Code, Community Design Element, and other regulations or administrative
  procedures.

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 6
   Policy LU-4.4: Economic Development. Support the development of commercial
  uses, both citywide and in strategic areas that strengthen the economy.

  Policy LU-4.5: Balanced Growth. Direct land uses and community growth in a
  manner that is consistent with community-wide goals and is consistent with the
  vision of the General Plan.

  Policy C-6.4: Parking Supply. Require residential, commercial, industrial, and other
  land uses in the community to provide adequate onsite parking for their respective
  uses; allow for joint-use parking provided the parking needs of individual uses are
  satisfied.

Zoning Code Consistency
The site is zoned M-1 (Light Manufacturing). Pursuant to EMMC Section 17.123
(Conditional and Minor Use Permits) and 17.40.030 (Permitted Uses) minor vehicle repair
uses may be permitted with an approved MUP within the M-1 zone and are subject to the
specific provision for vehicle repair uses listed under EMMC 17.112.200. The applicant
has pursued a lot merger in order to meet the minimum lot frontage and size; therefore,
the proposed use meets the current development standards.

CITY REVIEW PROCESS:

Staff and other City Departments and Divisions have reviewed the project through the
City’s internal review process. This review process enables the various City Departments
and Divisions (i.e., Planning, Building, Public Works/Engineering, and Police) to review
development proposals for conformity with the provisions established in the EMMC.
Additionally, the review process ensures that each development proposal is designed to
be compatible with any existing structures onsite and/or the neighboring properties. The
concerns and/or conditions of all reviewing parties are included in the recommended
conditions of approval. Public notices were mailed to all property owners within a 300-foot
radius of the subject property.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW:

In accordance with the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
of 1970, as amended, this project is Categorically Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301
(Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, as amended.

FINDING OF FACT:

In order to approve the project, the Zoning Review Committee is required to make certain
findings. Section 17.123.040 (EMMC) – Necessary conditions outline the five (5) required
findings and conditions to be met in order to approve any Minor Use. Additionally, Section
17.120.050 (EMMC) – Outlines the five (5) guidelines to determine if the request is
appropriate for granting of all Zoning Clearances;

Necessary Findings for Minor Use Permit

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 7
 FINDING:

  A. The Minor Use Permit will not be detrimental to the public health, safety or welfare
  or injurious to the subject property or other improvements in the vicinity;

FACT:

  The Applicant is requesting a Minor Use Permit (MUP) to establish an auto repair
  facility within an existing 4,800 square-foot commercial building. Presently, the
  business is intended to operate Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
  and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. The proposed business will conduct all vehicle
  repair services within the existing building, ensuring any noise generated will be
  minimized. In addition, the subject site is surrounded by industrial and commercial
  uses on all sides, meaning no residential properties will be affected by potential
  generated noise. The subject site has the required parking spaces for the use and
  has provided waiting areas/storage area for vehicle waiting to be serviced, ensuring
  no business activity will encroach into the public-right-of-way. The auto repair
  business has no identifiable negative impacts, such as noise, odor, or excessive
  trash waste, that would be detrimental to the public health, safety or welfare or
  injurious to the subject property or other improvements in the vicinity.

FINDING:

  B. The proposed use applied for at the location indicated is one for which a Minor Use
  permit is authorized;

FACT:

  The subject site is located within the M-1 (Light Manufacturing) zoning district which
  allows for the proposed “Vehicle Repair-Minor” use with an approved Minor Use
  Permit.

FINDING:

  C. The subject property for the proposed use is adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate such use and that all yards, spaces, walls, fences, parking, loading,
  landscaping and other features required for the proposed use are provided;

FACT:

  The Applicant is requesting a Minor Use Permit to operate a vehicle repair facility
  within an existing commercial building. The proposed business meets all on-site
  parking requirements and specific provisions for vehicle repair uses. Based on
  Staff’s assessment, the proposed vehicle repair facility meets requirements of the
  EMMC. No additional square footage or alterations are proposed to the existing
  structure and site; therefore, the property is found to be adequate in size and shape
  to accommodate the proposed use.

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 8
 FINDING:

  D. The subject property abuts streets and highways adequate in width and pavement
  type to carry the kind of traffic which will be generated by the proposed use;

FACT:

  The subject property abuts Tyler Avenue with ingress/egress provided from one (1)
  existing driveway to access the parking area. According to the City’s General Plan,
  Tyler Avenue is secondary arterial, typically intended to carry traffic from one part
  of the community to another and connect to major arterials. Tyler Avenue fulfills the
  standard design requirements for their classification and can accommodate the
  amount and intensity of traffic that the vehicle repair business would generate.

FINDING:

  E. The Minor Use Permit is consistent with the purpose, goals, and policies of the
  City’s General Plan, Zoning Code, and any applicable Specific Plan.

FACT:

  The proposed project is consistent with the City’s 2011 General Plan which
  designates the subject site as “Industrial Business Park”. Policy LU-4.4 and 4.5
  support the development of the “Vehicle Repair- Minor” use to strengthen the
  economy. The subject site is located within the M-1 (Light Manufacturing) zone
  which allows for the proposed use with an approved Minor Use Permit. Therefore,
  the granting of a Minor Use Permit will not adversely affect the purpose, goals, and
  policies of the General Plan.

Guidelines for Director Level Zoning Clearance

GUIDELINE:

  A. The proposed improvements will not be detrimental to the public health, safety or
  welfare or injurious to the subject property or other improvements in the area;

FACT:

  The requested DLZC is meant to ensure futures use for the adjacent parcel to the
  north (APN: 8104-019-005) will have access to the public right-of-way from the
  subject site and adequate on-site parking for future use. In conjunction with the
  Minor Use Permit, the proposed improvements will not be detrimental to public
  health, safety, or welfare, nor injurious to the subject property.

GUIDELINE:

  B. The orientation and location of the buildings or structures are appropriate for the
  property;

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 9
 FACT:

  The requested items will not alter the orientation of existing structures on either
  parcel. A tenant improvement is proposed on the subject site to install equipment
  associated with the vehicle repair business.

GUIDELINE:

  C. The vehicular and pedestrian circulation on the property allow for the safe
  movement of people regardless of their mode of travel;

FACT:

  The request of the DLZC will establish shared access to the public right-of-way and
  parking for the adjacent parcel from the subject site. In conjunction with the Minor
  Use Permit findings and Condition of Approval No. 25, the property will allow for the
  safe movement of people regardless of their mode of travel.

GUIDELINE:

  D. The functionality of the floor plans is superior; and

FACT:

  This request is made in conjunction with a Minor Use Permit request. Therefore,
  this finding is not applicable in that the scope of this DLZC request is to establish
  shared access and parking with the adjacent north parcel.

GUIDELINE:

  E. The scale, character and quality of the improvements are consistent with purpose,
  goals and policies of the City’s General Plan, Zoning Code, any applicable Specific
  Plan and its Comprehensive Design Guidelines.

FACT:

  In conjunction with the requested Minor Use Permit, the granting of the Director
  Level Zoning Clearance advances the purpose, goals, and policies of the General
  Plan. Land Use Policy 4.4 will be met by providing alternative parking allowances
  for a future tenant on the adjacent parcel. Further Circulation Policy 6.4 will be met
  by providing joint-use parking for multiple uses.

RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends that the Zoning Review Committee evaluate the proposal and consider
the following Actions:

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 10
   A. Adopt a Categorical Exemption Under Article 19, Class 1, Section 15301 (Existing
  Facilities) pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act and Guidelines; and

  B. Adopt the finding of Facts to approve MUP No. 15-2025 and DLZC No.13-2026,
  subject to the conditions of approval

ATTACHMENTS:

  1. Conditions of Approval
  2. Project Plans
  3. Letter of Intent
  4. Public Hearing Notice, Radius Map and Site Posting

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 11
 ATTACHMENT NO. 1- CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL:

Staff recommend that the Zoning Review Committee hereby approve MUP No. 15-2025,
and DLZC No.13-2026 for the Project in accordance with the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) of 1970 and the CEQA Guidelines, as amended, subject to the
following conditions:

  1. The approval of MUP No. 15-2025 to establish a general auto repair and
  maintenance services (Vehicle Repair, Minor) use at 2517 Tyler Avenue. Including
  DLZC No.13-2026 to establish shared access and parking with the adjacent
  northern parcel.

  2. The project shall substantially conform to MUP No. 15-2025, DLZC No.13-2026 and
  the project plans on file with the City Planning Division and as presented to the
  Zoning Review Committee on July 14, 2026.

  3. Approval of MUP No. 15-2025 and DLZC No.13-2026 shall be effective for a period
  of 24 months from the approval effective date; provided however, that prior to such
  a date, building permits and a business license shall have been obtained, or an
  extension shall have been approved.

  4. A copy of the conditions of approval shall be printed and attached to any project
  plans related to this approval and submitted to the Building and Safety Division
  during the plan check process, if applicable.

  5. All applicable conditions shall be met or deemed to have been addressed by the
  Community & Economic Development Director or designee prior to final inspection.

  6. All Planning Division standards and conditions shall be complied with prior to the
  issuance of the Business License or at another time specified in the conditions of
  approval or as outlined in City Codes.

  7. Prior to clearance for Building and Safety Plan check from the Planning Division,
  the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with the conditions of approval in writing
  to the project planner.

LEGAL

  8. Adherence to the entitlement conditions of approval shall be demonstrated at all
  times. A failure to comply may be cause for a review by the Planning Commission
  for potential revision or revocation of the approvals herein pursuant to EMMC
  §17.10.140 (Revocation of Permits).

  9. By acceptance of the approval of the project by the City, the Applicant shall defend,
  indemnify, and hold harmless the City and its agents, officers, and employees from
  any claim, action, or proceeding against the City or its agents, officers, and
  employees to challenge, set aside, void or annul the approval of the project from an
  action which may be brought within the time period provided for such actions or

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 12
   challenges under applicable law. The City shall promptly notify the Applicant of any
  claim, action, or proceeding and the City shall cooperate in any such defense.
SIGNAGE

  10. The approval of any business signage shall be under a separate permit. All signs
  shall be reviewed and approved by the Planning Division.

  11. Prior to the occupancy of the building, no person shall erect, alter, repair, or relocate
  any sign without obtaining a Sign Permit from the Planning Division. All signs shall
  be reviewed to determine whether the proposed sign is consistent with the
  requirements of EMMC Chapter 17.80.

  12. Banners are prohibited onsite at all times with the exception of banners that are
  approved with a Temporary Sign Permit by the Planning Division. Attachment of
  non-city approved signs, banners, product signs, or advertisements to light
  poles/standards on or off-site is prohibited at all times.

MAINTENANCE

  13. The site and the public R.O.W. adjacent to any portions of the site, shall be kept
  free of weeds, trash, or other debris, and that abandoned vehicles be promptly
  reported, pursuant to the Municipal Code and Los Angeles County Fire and Health
  Codes at all times.

  14. All onsite parking spaces shall be accessible and free of obstruction and can only
  be used for parking of operable vehicles at all times

  15. All public exit and entry doors to the building shall be maintained in a working
  conditions and must be cleared for use during business hours at all times.

  16. All entitlements and permits approved by the City Council, Planning Commission,
  Zoning Review Committee or Community Development Director (and Public Works
  Director for permits issued for items in the public right-of-way) shall remain in full
  force and effect as long as the use, building or structure remains in operation. Any
  entitlement granted pursuant to EMMC Title 17 is transferable and assignable;
  however, all successors in interest shall abide by all of the original conditions. Any
  entitlement or permit granted by aforementioned reviewing body may be revoked
  or revised for cause if any of the conditions of approval, terms with the maintenance
  agreement, or terms of the permit are violated or if any law or ordinance is violated,
  pursuant to Section 17.10.040 (EMMC).

  17. All activities on the property shall comply with the City of El Monte Noise Ordinance
  at all times.

OPERATION STANDARDS:

  18. The Applicant shall submit a Business Occupancy Permit application and letter of
  intent for the new use and shall comply with El Monte Licensing Division
  requirements.

  MUP NO. 15-2025 &DLZC NO. 13-2026 | 2517 Tyler Avenue | 13
   19. All work on vehicles shall be conducted within an enclosed building.

  20. Vehicles awaiting service or pick-up shall be stored within an enclosed building or
  in a designated on-site parking area. Unattended vehicles shall not be parked or
  stored in required customer parking spaces, within the public right-of-way, or off-
  site on a separate property.

  21. Exterior storage, including tires, shall be fully screened from all property lines by
  building walls and/or screen walls.

  22. The hours of operation shall be limited to between 7:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. daily.

  23. The property owner shall remove any graffiti on the Subject Property within 24 hours
  of discovery. The paint utilized to cover the graffiti must substantially match the
  existing structure. In the event that the paint finish of the abated area is noticeably
  distinguishable from the rest of the structure, the property owner shall paint
  additional portions of the building to minimize the disparity, subject to the
  approval of the Planning Division. Original surface materials installed and
  designed to not accept paint material such as stone, metal, veneers, etc. shall be
  restored to original finish with methods accepted and agreed to by the Planning
  Division.

FENCING

  24. Remove unpermitted panel fencing along front, interior, and property line. All
  fencing shall comply with fencing provisions for nonresidential uses listed under
  EMMC 17.60.120.

LANDSCAPING

  25. Front landscaping shall be maintained in an orderly and healthy condition.

PARKING AND ACCESS AGREEMENT

  25. A covenant shall be recorded on the subject site and the property immediately
  abutting to the north of the subject site to ensure shared parking and vehicular
  access to the public right of way. Such covenant shall be prepared to the
  satisfaction of the City Attorney. This requirement would demonstrate a parking
  agreement between the subject site and the adjacent site.

  26. Verification of continued service shall be submitted to the Planning Division by
  January 1st of each year.

BUILDING AND SAFETY

  27. Project shall comply with 2025 California Building & Fire Codes, and El Monte
  Municipal Code. Exterior ADA requirements, EV charges, and landscaping
  structural details shall be shown on construction plans, not landscaping plans.

REQUEST: The Applicant requests approval of MUP No. 15-2025 to establish a vehicle repair facility

general auto repair and maintenance services – within an existing 4,800 square-foot commercial building.

northern parcel. The subject site is 19,200 square feet in area and located in the M-1 (Light
Manufacturing) zone. The Minor Use Permit and Director Level Zoning Clearance request is made
pursuant to Chapter 17.123 (Conditional and Minor Use Permits) and Chapter 17.120 (Zoning
Clearances) of the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC).
